pipeline_name: Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage System (EGTS)

validity.recommendation: note the ~4% Capacity discrepancy against EIA's incremental-capacity figure; otherwise no change needed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook carries this exact project ('Morgantown Connector Project', operator 'Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage', FERC pre-filing docket PF21-3) across every release from 2021-10 (first appearance, status 'Pre-applied', last-updated 2021-08-17) through 2026-08 (status 'Cancelled' since the 2022-01 release, last-updated 2022-01-14). A general-web search also surfaced a company fact-sheet titled 'Morgantown Connector Project' hosted at bhegts.com describing the same scope (up to 220,000 Dth/d for Monongalia County, WV customers, with 4 new compressor stations in Clinton/Centre/Franklin Counties PA and Loudoun County VA) -- consistent with the EIA record -- but that specific asset URL now 404s and has no Wayback capture (checked CDX for bhegts.com/*morgantown*: zero captures), so it is not citable; noted here as corroborating context only, not staged as a ref. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission expansion (Authority=FERC in EIA), matches the sheet's Fuel=Gas / commodity. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's other two EGTS in-scope rows (P3169 Mid-Atlantic Chiller, P7825 Capital Area) -- EIA carries all three as separate named projects with separate dockets/scopes/counties; not the same physical facilities. NAME-COLLISION HAZARD (not a duplicate, flagging for future researchers): a completely unrelated 'Morgantown Connector' pipeline exists -- Hope Gas's ~30-mile local distribution line from Wadestown to Osage, WV, filed with the WV PSC in 2023 and placed in service ~2026 (Dominion Post / Marcellus Drilling News, May 2026 and Mar 2026) -- built by a different company (Hope Gas, a CenterPoint Energy subsidiary) for a different purpose (LDC system reliability, not FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission) under no relationship to EGTS's cancelled PF21-3 project. Multiple search results conflated the two; confirmed via EIA's docket/operator fields and the WV PSC filing date (2023, i.e. after EGTS's project was already cancelled in Jan 2022) that they are unrelated. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 'Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage Inc' at 100% is consistent with EGTS's own SEC 10-Q (filed 2022-09-06, CIK 1936737), which states EGTS's own stock is 100% held by its parent Eastern Energy Gas Holdings LLC (an indirect wholly-owned Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary) -- i.e. EGTS is a single-entity subsidiary with no joint-venture partners, consistent with a 100% Owner1 record for its own projects; that filing does not name the Morgantown Connector project specifically, so it supports the ownership STRUCTURE claim, not a project-specific one. SPEC: Length (21 mi) and SegmentCost ($190.8M) match EIA exactly; Status/CancelledYear match (EIA shows Cancelled by the 2022-01 release, consistent with the sheet's 2022); Capacity is close but not exact -- sheet 250.00 MMcf/d vs EIA's Additional Capacity 240.00 MMcf/d, a ~4% difference that is larger than a simple rounding gap. Only one origin (EIA) has any capacity figure for this cancelled pre-filing project; searched for a second source (FERC eLibrary docket PF21-3 -- the docketsheet is a JS-rendered Angular app that returns no static content to curl/wget and the project never advanced to a public application filing, so no FERC order exists to check; Federal Register full-text search for 'Morgantown Connector' and 'PF21-3' returned zero results, consistent with a project that never left pre-filing) and found none, so this stays flagged rather than silently resolved. Recommend keeping the sheet's 250.00 unless/until a second source is found; noting EIA's 240.00 as the contested candidate.

verifications.note: EIA Oct 2021 release, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', Excel row 86: Morgantown Connector Project first appears, Status 'Pre-applied', Last Updated Date 2021-08-17. Not present in any earlier release (checked back to Jan 2021 and Jul 2021 in the flattened history).

fills.researcher_notes: FERC docket number PF21-3 (a pre-filing docket, numbered by filing year) plus EIA's first appearance of the project in the Oct 2021 release (last-updated 2021-08-17, status Pre-applied) together support ProposalYear=2021. Left ProposalMonth blank -- EIA's 'last updated' date is EIA's own record-keeping date, not necessarily the FERC pre-filing request date, so I did not infer a specific month. Searched FERC eLibrary and Federal Register for the actual pre-filing request date; neither returned usable results (eLibrary's docketsheet is JS-rendered; Federal Register had zero hits, consistent with a project that never reached the application/FR-notice stage).

No construction ever occurred. EIA shows the project moving directly from 'Pre-applied' (Oct 2021) to 'Cancelled' (Jan 2022) -- it never advanced to a certificate application, so no construction start date exists. Searched FERC eLibrary and Federal Register for any notice of construction authorization; none found (consistent with a pre-filing-stage cancellation).

Project cancelled at the pre-filing stage before construction or certification; it never entered service, so there is no in-service date to source. EIA's 'Year In Service Date' field for this project is 'na' in every release.

verifications.note: EIA Aug 2026 release, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', row 1136, Status 'Cancelled'. The status flip is bounded between the 2021-10 release (Pre-applied) and the 2022-01 release (Cancelled, last-updated 2022-01-14).

fills.researcher_notes: The sheet's CancelledYear=2022 is consistent with EIA's own history: still 'Pre-applied' in the Oct 2021 release, 'Cancelled' with last-updated 2022-01-14 in the Jan 2022 release -- so the cancellation happened sometime between roughly Aug 2021 and Jan 2022, and could plausibly be late 2021 rather than 2022. Single-source; no FERC order or press report of the withdrawal was found (see Status fill note) to pin the exact month.

Project Notes: 'Project to provide up to 220,000 dekatherms per day...' (220,000 Dth/d ~= 227 MMcf/d at standard heat content, closer to EIA's 240 than to the sheet's 250).

fills.researcher_notes: Kept the sheet's recorded 250.00 MMcf/d since only one source (EIA, 240.00) was found and it does not exactly match; filed as a spec concern in validity[] with contested={"Capacity":"240.00"} rather than silently overriding. Note the project's own 220,000 Dth/d description (see Project Notes) converts to roughly 227 MMcf/d, which sits between the two figures and does not cleanly resolve the discrepancy either way.
No MAOP/pressure figure exists for this project in EIA (field not tracked) or anywhere else found -- it never reached a certificate application or tariff filing where design pressure would be stated.

EIA's own 'Pipeline Diameter (Inches)' field is blank for this project in every release -- EIA has no data either. No other primary source (FERC application, operator engineering summary) exists since the project stayed in pre-filing and never filed a certificate application with design specs.

No document discloses an upstream gas source for this project specifically. EGTS's broader Appalachian system draws on Marcellus/Utica production, but attaching that system-level fact to this cancelled pre-filing segment would be the aggregate-vs-segment error the SOP warns against, so left blank rather than forced.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status is correctly cancelled and stays cancelled through EIA's most recent (Aug 2026) release -- no revival evidence found. Searched specifically for a revival (the way NESE and North Brooklyn revived): no news, filing, or docket reopening for 'Morgantown Connector' or PF21-3 in Federal Register, FERC eLibrary web search, or general press from 2022 through 2026. Distinguished this from the unrelated, unaffiliated 'Hope Gas Morgantown Connector' LDC line (WV PSC filing 2023, in service 2026) which is a different project by a different company for a different purpose -- see validity note. ShelvedCancelledType is currently blank on the sheet and should be set to 'inferred' (no FERC order or press release of the withdrawal was found -- only EIA's own status-history bounds the cancellation between Aug 2021 and Jan 2022), per the batch guidance for cancelled rows with no type recorded.

summary: P4452 EGTS Morgantown Connector Project confirmed real and correctly cancelled (EIA docket PF21-3, dropped in pre-filing between Oct 2021 and Jan 2022); Length/Cost/Location/Status exact-match EIA, Capacity flagged as a ~4% spec discrepancy (sheet 250 vs EIA 240, single source only). Distinguished from an unrelated same-named Hope Gas LDC project. ConstructionYear/StartYear1/Pressure/Diameter/FuelSource genuinely UNRESOLVED (project never left pre-filing).
